messages:
maria: Ran a focused nsys + perfetto pass on the weird throughput drop from the long-seq workload. attached timeline: /tmp/nsys/deeptrace_2579.qdrep. saw a very regular HBM bandwidth waveform that aligns with KV page scans.

alex: can you paste the high-level timeline snippet? was this during batching ramp or steady-state?

maria: steady-state after warmup (~30s). here's trimmed NVTX stack we used: 
```
NVTX: decode->kv_lookup->kv_page_read->kernel_dispatch
kernel: attention_forward (chosen: aten_attn_v2)
```
pattern: every ~120ms HBM bw spikes to ~760 GB/s for ~10-12ms then falls to ~120 GB/s. correlates with large KV read sets when seq_len > 8192.

ryan: wow that's huge. sounds like repeated full-KV scans instead of incremental prefix hits. did kv cache hit-rate drop?

sophia: yep, hit-rate drops from 98% -> 64% when we cross the threshold, per the same trace. I think kernel selection made attention kernel that is heavy on memory reads (strided loads) for long sequences.

maria: confirmed. kernel selector picked aten_attn_v2 for long seqs because it reports better FLOPS for that path. but aten_attn_v2 uses an uncoalesced gather for KV pages which thrashes HBM.

perf-bot: Profiling hint: try aten_attn_v2 with kv_prefetch=1 or fall back to aten_attn_baseline for sequences > 4096 to reduce HBM peak.

alex: did you try enabling microbatch adaptive batching? that might shrink per-batch KV working set and reduce peaks.

maria: tried microbatching (mb=4) — reduced peak by ~20% but increased latency. tradeoff is expected. interestingly, if we also enable prefix caching for 2nd token groups, hit-rate jumps back to ~92% and bandwidth stabilizes.

ryan: can you share the perfetto slice screenshot or a short flame? even a textual timeline helps.

maria: pasted minimal perfetto slice below (timeline condensed):
```
0ms: decode (2ms)
2-40ms: kv_lookup (20-30ms)
40-52ms: kernel_dispatch (attention_forward 12ms) -> HBM spike
52-120ms: token gen
repeat every token chunk
```

sophia: that kv_lookup window looks long. is the runtime doing per-token synchronous KV loads? we should batch those reads across microbatches.

maria: runtime config was continuous-batching=on but the batching heuristic chosen small batch depth because of latency SLO. need heuristic tweak: prefer slightly wider batching when predicted KV read set > X pages.

alex: propose change: compute expected_kv_pages = ceil((seq_len * beam * tokens_per_batch)/kv_page_items) at request admission and force batching_depth=min(max_depth, ceil(expected_kv_pages/target_pages)). If expected_kv_pages > 64, change kernel selection to aten_attn_baseline.

ryan: +1. also add an instrumentation counter that emits KV miss bursts per NVTX range so we can see correlation automatically in nsys.

maria: implemented quick patch on branch perf/kv-waveform. tests show HBM peak down to 420 GB/s and tail P99 latency improved by 14% on the problematic traces. pushing for canary tomorrow.

sophia: include an A/B run with and without kernel fallback; we need to ensure generation quality doesn't regress. add eval prompts used in the incident to the rollout gating.

perf-bot: Canary checklist: 1) KV-miss histogram 2) HBM-peak monitor 3) kernel-selection TTL 4) eval prompts pass.

maria: noted. will add metrics and start canary at 09:00 UTC. ping me if you want to watch the perfetto live session. :eyes:

alex: thanks. great catch — this feels like a kernel-selection + caching heuristics mismatch rather than a pure allocator bug.

ryan: one more: consider adding a small on-device prefetch coalescer that merges adjacent KV page reads into single DMA ops when the pattern is near-linear. could knock another ~10-15% off peaks.

maria: good idea, filing ticket perf/kv-coalesce-2579. attaching current nsys qdrep and perfetto trace to the ticket.

sophia: thanks team. low-effort change for big wins, love it. :rocket:
